Add recorded parent information to person histories

Source: R/get_parent_info.R
get_parent_info.Rd

Match mothers and fathers by person ID and append their ages at each child's birth and their optional recorded groups. All persons, including founders and deceased persons, retain their original row order and columns. The input population is not modified and no known endpoint is required.

Usage

get_parent_info(population)

Arguments

population

A validated hammel_population, such as the result of simulate().

Value

A separate tibble containing all person columns plus age_mother and age_father, measured at that person's birth. When groups are present, also group_mother and group_father. Empty populations retain the enriched column types.

Details

Ages are in continuous years: the child's birth time minus the parent's birth time. Unknown parents yield missing ages and groups. Group fields are omitted when persons has no group column; otherwise its type is preserved. These are recorded identities, not reconstructions of historical group transitions. Existing columns that conflict with the added fields cause an error.

Examples

population <- create_baseline_population(10)
get_parent_info(population)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 8
#>    person_id sex   birth_time death_time mother_id father_id age_mother
#>        <int> <chr>      <dbl>      <dbl>     <int>     <int>      <dbl>
#>  1         1 f          -41.1         NA        NA        NA         NA
#>  2         2 m          -61.6         NA        NA        NA         NA
#>  3         3 m          -15.1         NA        NA        NA         NA
#>  4         4 m          -24.4         NA        NA        NA         NA
#>  5         5 f          -65.2         NA        NA        NA         NA
#>  6         6 m          -61.2         NA        NA        NA         NA
#>  7         7 f          -69.6         NA        NA        NA         NA
#>  8         8 f          -13.7         NA        NA        NA         NA
#>  9         9 f          -17.0         NA        NA        NA         NA
#> 10        10 m          -57.5         NA        NA        NA         NA
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: age_father <dbl>
